text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Hosni Mubarak says in an interview with the Kuwaiti newspaper al-Siyassa that terrorism has been banished and Egypt enjoys the highest level of stability and security.
- Six journalists to be referred to court on charges of insulting and slandering the president's sons, Alaa and Gamal.
- Israeli Labour Party's Ehud Barak to visit Egypt on Tuesday at the head of a parliamentary delegation, which will hold talks with Egyptian officials.
- A speech by Mubarak will be delivered today at the conference "Islam and the West - Past, Present and Future" which opens in Cairo and lasts for four days.

- Renters' requests for new farm land, after their tenancy expired, have been accepted and a committee has settled 2,200 cases which arose as a result of the land law which takes effect in October. Financing of new land purchases has begun.
- Mubarak says in his interview with the Kuwaiti paper that a common Arab market will open borders and develop production.
- Egypt is trying to dislodge the peace process from its stalemate.
- China and Egypt are holding talks to set up a free trade zone in the Gulf of Suez.
